messages:
Jules H.: Ran into a weird installer collision today. I had redwoodctl installed via apt on my Ubuntu WSL and tried `snap install redwoodctl` to test the snap channel. Snap failed with: 

```
error: cannot install "redwoodctl": conflicting files in snap "redwoodctl" (redwoodctl: /usr/bin/redwoodctl already exists)
```

After the snap 'succeeds' the shell still runs the apt binary from /usr/bin and the versions disagree. Anyone hit this?

Marco P.: Yup. Snap vs apt fight is classic. Snap puts exec in /snap/bin and creates a shim in /usr/bin sometimes. If you previously installed via dpkg/apt the old binary stays. Quick fix: `sudo apt remove redwoodctl && sudo snap install redwoodctl --classic` then `hash -r` in your shell. Also check PATH order: /snap/bin should come before /usr/bin if you want snap first.

Jules H.: That fixed the path mixup. Two followups found while testing local dev flows: (1) running `redwoodctl dev --docker` inside a container that is headless tries SSO and blocks because it attempts to open a browser. There's no documented `--no-browser` in the packaged snap. (2) `redwoodctl login --token-stdin` worked in my host shell but in the container the CLI rejected the token with "stale session" after a minute because our dev environment auto-rotates tokens.

Ava L.: For (1) we added a tiny wrapper to our dev image: `export REDWOODCTL_NO_BROWSER=1` and use `redwoodctl login --token-file /secrets/redwood_token`. Would be nicer if the snap documented env knobs or exposed `--no-browser` in the older builds.

Marco P.: For (2) token rotation causing stale tokens is something we saw in prod too. CLI keeps a `~/.redwood/token_history` and sometimes replays old tokens if the active token isn't pinned to a profile id. Proposal: when rotating, CLI should prune history for that profile and persist only the latest, or store tokens in OS keystore instead of a file.

Jules H.: Filed issue with a tiny repro and included Dockerfile: it mounts ~/.redwood from host, then runs `redwoodctl login --token-stdin` with a token that immediately rotates on a background job. CLI saved both tokens and subsequent `redwoodctl whoami` failed because it tried the older token first.

CI-bot: pipeline #9012 failed: `redwoodctl login --profile ci` -> saved token to wrong profile when config had duplicate names; follow-up ticket in infra backlog.

Ava L.: Short-term workarounds we used: 1) in CI set `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG=/tmp/rdw-config-$$` per job to avoid shared configs, 2) `redwoodctl login --token-file /secrets/redwood_token && redwoodctl config set current_profile_id "$PROFILE_ID"` (we patched our image to accept profile ids). Both are ugly.

redwoodctl-bot: New issue created: #2699 "snap/apt installer collisions, headless docker SSO, and token history causing stale-playback" by Jules H. https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/2699

Marco P.: Action items: add installer note for snap/apt conflicts, expose `--no-browser`/`--token-stdin` in stable channels, and implement token-history pruning or keystore backend. I'll pick the docs PR, anyone wants the CLI patch?

Ava L.: I'll take the keystore proof-of-concept (macOS Keychain + gnome-keyring) and drop a design in the issue. Thanks! :raised_hands:
